newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian president was on artifical respirator.
newsitem.headline: Austrian president was on artifical respirator.

text.p: Austrian President Thomas Klestil regained consciousness on Monday after spending three days sedated and on an artificial respirator, his doctors said, lifting a veil of secrecy around the president's illness.

Klestil, 63, was admitted to Vienna General Hospital on September 13 suffering from an aggressive and atypical form of pneumonia. A virtual news blackout had sparked media speculation that his condition was graver than first thought.
Speaking at a hastily convened news conference on Monday, Klestil's doctors said they had transferred their patient to intensive care at the end of last week after his condition deteriorated.
They were still awaiting the results of a lung biopsy performed on Friday.
"The president was sedated and on an artificial respirator from the time of the biopsy until this morning," said lung specialist Professor Wolfgang Graninger.
"The results are not through but we have been able to eliminate many illnesses. The president's condition is not life threatening," he continued.
Senior doctor Professor Josef Smolen said there was no evidence of cancer.
"We can say with certainty there is no carcenoma...although we do not know the precise form of the inflammation," he said.

Klestil's spokesman Heinz Nussbaumer confirmed that Chancellor Franz Vranitzky had taken on the president's duties but said the transfer of power had not taken place until Monday, when Klestil regained consciousness.
"The president is capable of carrying out his duties but he preferred to ask the chancellor to take over," Nussbaumer said.
Klestil's role in Austrian politics is that of a figurehead. The chancellor is the head of government.
Nussbaumer deflected questions about the delay in informing the public about the president's illness and said he had been unaware of Klestil's condition over the weekend.
"I spoke with the president on Thursday (before the biopsy) and was in contact with the hospital again on Sunday," he said.
Klestil became president in 1992 and helped restore Austria's image on the international stage after succeeding Kurt Waldheim, who was shunned for concealing his wartime past.

Klestil first sought medical attention in July shortly after a trip to Turkey. He had complained of inflammation of his joints, Smolen said. He later noted changes to his skin and earlier this month developed a fever and lung inflammation.
"Initial treatment was effective but the problem flared up again suddenly," Graninger said.
The doctors declined to forecast when Klestil would be able to go home but said they hoped to have more idea within the next three days.
